chunks: From him, from ʿUbays, from Ḥammād, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm, who said:
I heard al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام while he was saying:

Indeed, the beginning of the time of zuhr is the sun’s decline from the meridian, and the end of its time is one qāmah from the decline. And the beginning of the time of ʿasr is one qāmah, and the end of its time is two qāmahs. I said: Is it the same in winter and summer? He said: Yes. Then if it is said: We see that you have arranged the times one after another, and you have given some of them excellence over others, while it has been narrated that all of that is equal.

key_terms.أَوَّلَ وَقْتِ الظُّهْرِ: the beginning of the prescribed time for zuhr prayer
key_terms.أَوَّلَ وَقْتِ الْعَصْرِ: the beginning of the prescribed time for ʿasr prayer
key_terms.الْأَوْقَاتَ: the prayer times being ordered and distinguished from one another
key_terms.زَوَالُ الشَّمْسِ: the sun’s passing from the meridian, marking the onset of zuhr
key_terms.قَامَةٌ: a measured interval used here to define prayer time limits
key_terms.قَامَتَانِ: two measured intervals marking the end of ʿasr time in this report

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the beginning and end of the times of zuhr and ʿasr prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith states the beginning and end points for the times of zuhr and ʿasr, marking zuhr from the sun’s decline and ʿasr after a measured interval. It also affirms that this ruling applies equally in winter and summer, while raising the question of how these ordered times relate to reports indicating equality in the overall prayer times.
